title: Code stores Monday's tennis fact, and Thursday's prompt brings it back
subtitle: TunaTutor's real pipeline; the learner's lines and the greeting are made-up examples.

outcome.title: Thursday's greeting asks about the tennis match
lines: The model knows "tennis" only because the system prompt contains it, and it takes each stored fact as true.

captions.title: Monday, the backend resends the whole conversation
captions.text: The learner writes “Je joue au tennis…” (example). On every call the backend resends the system prompt and all the chat's messages, keyed by conversation ID, with the new message last.

captions.title: The model answers in JSON and proposes a fact
captions.text: The tutor answers in a fixed JSON shape: `responseText` to show, and `memoryUpdates`, usually empty. Here it holds set favorite_sport = tennis. The transcript keeps only `responseText`; bad JSON stores nothing.

captions.title: Code, not the model, decides whether this turn may write
captions.text: The gate reads state the app controls. With a story, a reference text or a reference picture attached (role-play), the turn queues no memory job. Here role-play is off, so the gate is open.

captions.title: Queue the fact in the same transaction as the messages
captions.text: The memory job row is written in the same transaction that saves the turn's messages, so both commit or neither does. The learner gets the reply text.

captions.title: A worker upserts the fact, one row per user and key
captions.text: A worker checks for pending jobs every second and claims one. It checks the memory switch, on by default, cleans the key and value, and upserts. A failing job is retried after 2, 4, 6 and 8 seconds.

captions.title: Thursday, the stored facts go back into the system prompt
captions.text: The new chat's transcript is empty. The backend loads the 50 most recently updated facts once and writes them as plain lines, such as “- favorite_sport: tennis”. The model asks about the match.
